key_insight: LLM2R turns 3D part assembly into a single-pass sequence modeling problem, using a pretrained decoder-only LLM with summary tokens to reason over all parts and predict every rigid pose at once.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster and more scalable reconstruction of fractured or disassembled 3D objects, especially when assemblies contain many parts and pairwise methods become inefficient.
method: Encode each part with Point-BERT + Q-Former into geometric token blocks.
Concatenate all part blocks and process them with a LoRA-adapted causal LLM in one forward pass.
Append learnable summary tokens so each part's pose head can fuse local and global context before predicting SE(3) transform.
evidence_signal: The method reports top performance across PartNet, PartNeXt, and Breaking Bad, with especially large gains as part count increases and strong zero-shot transfer to unseen categories.
watch_item: Because causal attention is directional, the model depends on the ordering of part blocks, so sequence design and token budget may affect robustness and reproducibility.
paper_title: LLM2R: From Large Language Models to 3D Reassemblers
